text:
Browser infrastructure for AI agents and web automation

 
 
 Stealth cloud browsers, a Playwright-based browser framework, and serverless functions to run your web automations 
 → Docs • Console • Anything API • Landing • Slack • X 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 

---

 What is Notte?

Notte gives AI agents and scripts a reliable browser. Drive cloud browser sessions with built-in stealth, CAPTCHA solving and proxies, or a local browser with the same API; deploy automations as functions; and keep credentials and identities out of your code. Read more in our documentation here 🔥

Choose your starting point:

 Product Use it for 
 --- --- 
 Notte CLI Drive browsers from the terminal, scripts or CI 
 Notte MCP Give your coding agent a cloud browser 
 Browser sessions Run Playwright or Puppeteer on stealth cloud browsers 
 Browser functions Deploy a browser script as an API or scheduled job 
 Anything API Turn a described task into a deployed API 
 Scraping Extract structured data from a page 

 Open-source core: 
- Local browser sessions → A Playwright-based browser that turns pages into actionable observations and clean markdown
- Scraping → Markdown, images or structured data (Pydantic models) from any page

 API service (recommended): 
- Stealth browser sessions → Hosted browsers with CAPTCHA solving, proxies and anti-detection, reachable over CDP from Playwright, Puppeteer or Selenium
- Functions → Deploy a Python automation and run it on demand, on a schedule, or behind an API endpoint
- Secrets vaults → Credential management for emails, passwords, MFA tokens, credit cards
- Digital personas → Identities with their own email, phone number and automated 2FA

 Coming from notte 1.9 or earlier? The agent loop ( notte.Agent , client.Agent , client.agents , AgentFallback ), workflows and local function execution were removed in 1.10. Use browser sessions from this SDK, the CLI or the MCP server to drive browsers, and Functions to deploy reusable automations.

 Quickstart

For JavaScript and TypeScript, see the Node SDK ( npm install notte-sdk ).

 

 Local sessions

Run a browser on your machine, observe the actions available on a page, execute them and scrape the result. No API key needed:

 

Structured scraping on a local session hands the page markdown to an extractor. Install the LLM extractor with pip install 'notte[llm]' and set OPENROUTER API KEY ; it defaults to google/gemini-3.5-flash-lite . You can also pass your own extractor with notte.Session(extractor=...) .

Set OPENROUTER API KEY to use OpenRouter with google/gemini-3.5-flash-lite by default.
For another OpenAI-compatible endpoint, set all three of NOTTE LLM BASE URL ,
 NOTTE LLM API KEY , and NOTTE LLM MODEL (the endpoint's own model ID):

- OpenAI: NOTTE LLM BASE URL= NOTTE LLM MODEL=gpt-4o .
- Gemini: NOTTE LLM BASE URL= NOTTE LLM MODEL=gemini-3.5-flash-lite .
- Ollama/custom: NOTTE LLM BASE URL= your local model ID, and NOTTE LLM API KEY=ollama for an unauthenticated local server. Ollama has not been live-tested.

 NOTTE LLM API KEY overrides OPENROUTER API KEY . The latter is used only at the default
OpenRouter URL, so it is never sent to a custom endpoint. The per-call model= argument
selects a model at the configured endpoint without translating its ID.

See notte-llm configuration for all settings.

 Natural-language actions

On a local session, act() runs one observe, decide and execute step from an instruction. choose() picks one
option about the current page and check() gives the probability that a statement about it holds. They need
 pip install 'notte[llm]' and OPENROUTER API KEY :

 

Values in variables replace {{name}} in typed text after the model call, so the model never sees them:
 session.act("type {{user}} in the username field", variables={"user": "standard user"}) . See the
act docs for dry runs, confidence thresholds and deciders.

 Cloud sessions

The API hosts the browser sessions for you and adds stealth, CAPTCHA solving, proxies, live view and recordings. Sign up on the Notte Console and create a free Notte API key 🔑

 

Every cloud session exposes a CDP endpoint, so you can keep your existing Playwright code ( pip install 'notte-sdk[playwright]' ):

 

 Session features

 Stealth

Built-in proxies, CAPTCHA solving and real Chrome browsers to get through bot detection.

 

For a custom proxy, set PROXY SERVER , PROXY USERNAME , and PROXY PASSWORD to your provider's connection details.

 

 File download / upload

Files uploaded to a session can be set on file inputs, and files downloaded by the browser are stored with the session.
Set UPLOAD FILE PATH to a local document and UPLOAD URL to a page with a file input.

 

 Cookies / Auth Sessions

Cookies provide a flexible way to authenticate your sessions. While we recommend using the secure vault for credential management, cookies offer an alternative approach for certain use cases.

 

 Bring your own browser

Point a session at any CDP-compatible browser (another provider, or a browser you run yourself) to use Notte's observe / execute / scrape on top of it. Set EXTERNAL CDP URL to the WebSocket URL of a running browser.

 

 Vaults

Store credentials in a vault and let the session fill them in: your code (and the LLMs that write it) only ever sees placeholders. Set GITHUB EMAIL and GITHUB PASSWORD to try it.

 

 Bitwarden on local sessions

A local session takes a vault object. AacVault asks your Bitwarden Password Manager for each login through Agent Access, and you approve every request in aac listen . Install aac v0.11.0, unlock your vault with /unlock in aac listen , then use /pair and set AAC TOKEN to its pairing token. Install the local browser with patchright install chromium .

 

 BitwardenVault (in notte core.credentials.bitwarden ) reads Bitwarden Secrets Manager with a machine account instead; install it with pip install "notte[bitwarden]" . See the Bitwarden integration for setup.

install.title: Quickstart
install.html:
For JavaScript and TypeScript, see the Node SDK (npm install notte-sdk).

pip install notte
patchright install --with-deps chromium

Local sessions

Run a browser on your machine, observe the actions available on a page, execute them and scrape the result. No API key needed:

import notte

with notte.Session(headless=True) as session:
    _ = session.execute(type="goto", url="https://www.notte.cc")
    obs = session.observe()
    print(obs.space.description)
    markdown = session.scrape(only_main_content=True)

Structured scraping on a local session hands the page markdown to an extractor. Install the LLM extractor with pip install 'notte[llm]' and set OPENROUTER_API_KEY; it defaults to google/gemini-3.5-flash-lite. You can also pass your own extractor with notte.Session(extractor=...).

Set OPENROUTER_API_KEY to use OpenRouter with google/gemini-3.5-flash-lite by default. For another OpenAI-compatible endpoint, set all three of NOTTE_LLM_BASE_URL, NOTTE_LLM_API_KEY, and NOTTE_LLM_MODEL (the endpoint's own model ID):

  • OpenAI: NOTTE_LLM_BASE_URL=https://api.openai.com/v1, NOTTE_LLM_MODEL=gpt-4o.
  • Gemini: NOTTE_LLM_BASE_URL=https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai, NOTTE_LLM_MODEL=gemini-3.5-flash-lite.
  • Ollama/custom: NOTTE_LLM_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434/v1, your local model ID, and NOTTE_LLM_API_KEY=ollama for an unauthenticated local server. Ollama has not been live-tested.

NOTTE_LLM_API_KEY overrides OPENROUTER_API_KEY. The latter is used only at the default OpenRouter URL, so it is never sent to a custom endpoint. The per-call model= argument selects a model at the configured endpoint without translating its ID.

See notte-llm configuration for all settings.

Natural-language actions

On a local session, act() runs one observe, decide and execute step from an instruction. choose() picks one option about the current page and check() gives the probability that a statement about it holds. They need pip install 'notte[llm]' and OPENROUTER_API_KEY:

import notte

with notte.Session(headless=True) as session:
    _ = session.execute(type="goto", url="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Main_Page")

    # one step per call; raises when no action fits the instruction
    result = session.act("type Ada Lovelace in the search box")
    print(result.status, result.operation, result.confidence)
    _ = session.act("open the Ada Lovelace article")

    choice = session.choose("What kind of page is this?", ["encyclopedia article", "online shop", "login page"])
    print(choice.choice, choice.probabilities)
    print(session.check("Is this page about a mathematician?"))

Values in variables replace {{name}} in typed text after the model call, so the model never sees them: session.act("type {{user}} in the username field", variables={"user": "standard_user"}). See the act docs for dry runs, confidence thresholds and deciders.

Cloud sessions

The API hosts the browser sessions for you and adds stealth, CAPTCHA solving, proxies, live view and recordings. Sign up on the Notte Console and create a free Notte API key 🔑

from notte_sdk import NotteClient

client = NotteClient()  # reads NOTTE_API_KEY

with client.Session(open_viewer=False) as session:
    _ = session.execute(type="goto", url="https://news.ycombinator.com")
    actions = session.observe(instructions="open the comments of the first post")
    if actions:
        _ = session.execute(actions[0])
    comments = session.scrape(only_main_content=True)

Every cloud session exposes a CDP endpoint, so you can keep your existing Playwright code (pip install 'notte-sdk[playwright]'):

from notte_sdk import NotteClient
from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright

client = NotteClient()

with client.Session(open_viewer=False) as session, sync_playwright() as p:
    browser = p.chromium.connect_over_cdp(session.cdp_url())
    page = browser.contexts[0].pages[0]
    _ = page.goto("https://www.notte.cc")
    print(page.title())

features.title: Session features
features.html:
Stealth

Built-in proxies, CAPTCHA solving and real Chrome browsers to get through bot detection.

from notte_sdk import NotteClient

client = NotteClient()

with client.Session(
    solve_captchas=True,
    proxies=True,  # US-based proxy
    browser_type="chrome",
) as session:
    _ = session.execute(type="goto", url="https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api2/demo")
    result = session.execute(type="captcha_solve", captcha_type="recaptcha", raise_on_failure=False)

For a custom proxy, set PROXY_SERVER, PROXY_USERNAME, and PROXY_PASSWORD to your provider's connection details.

import os
from notte_sdk import NotteClient
from notte_sdk.types import ExternalProxy

client = NotteClient()
proxy_settings = ExternalProxy(
    server=os.environ["PROXY_SERVER"],
    username=os.environ["PROXY_USERNAME"],
    password=os.environ["PROXY_PASSWORD"],
)

with client.Session(proxies=[proxy_settings]) as session:
    _ = session.execute(type="goto", url="https://www.notte.cc")

File download / upload

Files uploaded to a session can be set on file inputs, and files downloaded by the browser are stored with the session. Set UPLOAD_FILE_PATH to a local document and UPLOAD_URL to a page with a file input.

import os
from notte_sdk import NotteClient
from notte_sdk.types import FileSource

client = NotteClient()

with client.Session() as session:
    storage = session.storage
    uploaded_file = storage.upload(os.environ["UPLOAD_FILE_PATH"])

    _ = session.execute(type="goto", url=os.environ["UPLOAD_URL"])
    _ = session.execute(type="upload_file", selector="input[type=file]", file_path=uploaded_file.filename)

    # Download the files the browser downloaded (100 files per page)
    offset = 0
    while True:
        downloaded_files = storage.list(source=FileSource.SESSION_DOWNLOAD, offset=offset)
        for file in downloaded_files.files:
            storage.download(file_id=file.id, local_dir="./results")
        offset += len(downloaded_files.files)
        if offset >= downloaded_files.total or not downloaded_files.files:
            break

Cookies / Auth Sessions

Cookies provide a flexible way to authenticate your sessions. While we recommend using the secure vault for credential management, cookies offer an alternative approach for certain use cases.

from notte_sdk import NotteClient
import json

client = NotteClient()

# Upload cookies for authentication
cookies = [
    {
        "name": "sb-db-auth-token",
        "value": "base64-cookie-value",
        "domain": "github.com",
        "path": "/",
        "expires": 9778363203.913704,
        "httpOnly": False,
        "secure": False,
        "sameSite": "Lax"
    }
]

with client.Session() as session:
    session.set_cookies(cookies=cookies)  # or cookie_file="path/to/cookies.json"
    _ = session.execute(type="goto", url="https://github.com/nottelabs/notte")

    # Get cookies from the session
    cookies_resp = session.get_cookies()
    with open("cookies.json", "w") as f:
        json.dump(cookies_resp, f)

Bring your own browser

Point a session at any CDP-compatible browser (another provider, or a browser you run yourself) to use Notte's observe / execute / scrape on top of it. Set EXTERNAL_CDP_URL to the WebSocket URL of a running browser.

import os
from notte_sdk import NotteClient

client = NotteClient()
cdp_url = os.environ["EXTERNAL_CDP_URL"]

with client.Session(cdp_url=cdp_url, proxies=False, viewport_width=None, viewport_height=None) as session:
    _ = session.execute(type="goto", url="https://www.notte.cc/pricing")
    pricing = session.scrape(instructions="extract the pricing plans")
